claims.text: The starting material is a single-phase solid-solution titanium–nickel-based high-entropy alloy.
Friction stir processing at approximately 500°C can induce dynamic recrystallization in the alloy.
Suitable feed rate, rotation speed, and cooling rate can avoid detrimental residual stresses during processing.
Suitable friction-stir-processing parameters can prevent unwanted phase transformations.
Friction stir processing followed by rapid cooling will refine the alloy's grain structure.
The intervention will produce a high density of grain boundaries.
The intervention will cause solute segregation at grain boundaries.
Solute segregation will stabilize the refined grain boundaries at elevated temperature.
The refined grain structure will strengthen the alloy through the Hall–Petch effect.
The processed grain-boundary structure will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperatures.
The processed grain-boundary structure will impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperatures.
The FSP-treated alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
The FSP-treated alloy will have greater elevated-temperature ductility than the as-cast alloy.
The FSP-treated alloy will have better elevated-temperature creep resistance than the as-cast alloy.
The intervention is applicable to testing at temperatures up to 700°C in inert or controlled atmospheres.
A yield-strength and ductility improvement of approximately 10% or more is the proposed criterion for a successful intervention.
